newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end 2.80 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end 2.80 percent higher.

text.p: Pakistani stocks soared on Monday amid blue-chip buying powered by a rise in synthetic fibre prices and some good corporate results, dealers said.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index rose 40.81 points, or 2.80 percent, to end at 1,499.97. Gainers led losers 142 to 89. Turnover rose to 34.97 million shares from 25.12 million on Sunday.
The sharp jump in volumes shows that a lot of speculative trading has taken place and most players will like to book profits at these levels, the dealers said.
Bank of Punjab rose 1.80 rupees to 17.40, Adamjee Insurance 5.0 to 95, Dewan Salman Fibre 3.0 to 38.40, Pakistan Synthetic 2.0 to 15.50 and Dhan Fibres 1.05 to 5.75.
Hub Power Co rose 1.05 to 35.40, Pakistan State Oil 33 to 380 and National Refinery 3.25 to 33.25. PTCL rose 0.10 to 32.50 and ICI Pakistan rose 0.80 to 19.20.
